outcome: GRH itself remains fully open with no resolution, disproof, or narrowing of the existential question; the only movement in the window is ordinary analytic-number-theory progress on zero-density and equivalence results for Dirichlet L-functions, all human-authored with no AI involvement, alongside one non-credible self-published 'AI-assisted proof' claim that never reached arXiv or gained any expert traction.
summary: Since the 26 January 2024 frozen revision, GRH — do the nontrivial zeros of all Dirichlet L-functions lie on the critical line 1/2+it — remains open, and I found no credible claim to the contrary. The Wikipedia article itself (fetched live, not the frozen revision, purely to check whether its lead now records any change) has not been updated with any 2024-2026 development and still describes GRH as unproven outside the algebraic function-field case; its most recent cited item (Dunn-Radziwill, 2021) predates the window. Two lines of genuine, human-authored analytic number theory moved bounds relevant to GRH within the window, both counting as `progress` rather than `partial` or `resolved` because they narrow error terms or establish conditional equivalences without settling any case of the existential question: (1) Bin Chen, 'Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, and the density of zeros of Dirichlet's L-functions' (arXiv:2507.08296, submitted 11 July 2025, revised July 2026), which extends the Guth-Maynard large-value-estimate method (originally for the Riemann zeta function) to Dirichlet L-functions and improves the zero-density exponent from Huxley's 12/5 to 7/3 — an unconditional bound on how many zeros of Dirichlet L-functions can lie off the critical line at a given height, not a proof that none do. No AI system is mentioned anywhere in the abstract or accessible metadata. (2) Kohji Suzuki, arXiv:2508.17701 ('Detecting zeros of Dirichlet L-functions via the Riemann zeta-function', August 2025), which — conditional on the ordinary Riemann Hypothesis — proves an equivalence between a distributional property of zeta zeros and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions. This is a related/conditional structural result, not unconditional progress toward or against GRH, and per §3.1 would not by itself move the classification; it is the triage's own found item and I confirm its characterization. I also investigated a self-published item the triage's queries did not surface: M. Sghiar's ResearchGate posting 'A Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis Assisted by Artificial Intelligence: An Analytic Approach' (and an earlier 'Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis by ChatGPT'), which explicitly claims ChatGPT assistance in deriving a purported proof. This item never appeared on arXiv, has no journal acceptance, no expert digestion, and no evidence of even preliminary community engagement beyond the author's own postings — it sits alongside a long-running genre of crank RH proofs (Sghiar himself and others have posted many such claims over years). Because it never gained traction, was never checked by anyone besides the author, and concerns RH/GRH generally rather than being a distinct dated event that was 'announced then withdrawn', it does not meet the bar for `claimed` (no expert or institutional uptake at all) and does not fit `incident` cleanly either (nothing was ever accepted enough to need withdrawing). I record it here as color rather than as the event the status rests on; it does not change the classification. Net: the correct classification is `progress` (a real, human-only bound moved) rather than `open`/`no_change_found`, and `ai_role` is `none` because no AI system contributed to any result that actually changed the mathematical record — the only AI-attributed claim never entered the corpus of accepted results.
competing_reading: One could argue the status should be `open` with `no_change_found` true, treating Bin Chen's zero-density improvement as too incremental or too far from the existential GRH question (an 'are there any off-line zeros' question, which per §3.1's rule that record/bound movements don't count for existence questions might seem excluded). I read `progress` as correct because §3.1's exclusion is specifically for record-of-largest-known-object or verified-search-limit style non-events, whereas a zero-density theorem is a genuine analytic bound of the kind §6.1 explicitly assigns to `progress` ('a bound moved'). If a stricter reading is preferred, the honest fallback is `open` with `no_change_found` true and this progress noted as context that does not itself count.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the pipeline's status taxonomy treats an unconditional zero-density exponent improvement for the exact L-function family in the bullet's statement as a qualifying 'bound moved' (favoring `progress`) or as insufficiently connected to the existential question to count at all (favoring `open`/`no_change_found`).
